oewn-07466684-n.learner: the social occasion at which two people are married
examples: The wedding took place: the bride and bridegroom set off for Kent from the church door.
Mr. Darcy had been at her sister's wedding.

oewn-01039028-n.learner: the act of getting married, or the ceremony in which it is done
examples: The wedding was performed by an old clergyman in a small country church.

oewn-08273656-n.learner: the group of people who are gathered at a wedding
examples: The whole wedding party walked back from the church to the house together.

oewn-06381452-n.learner: a made-up piece of writing that tells a set of connected events
examples: hardly a character, hardly an incident could be retrenched without loss to the story
it connects itself in the strictest way with the course of the story earlier

oewn-07235754-n.learner: a telling of the details of an act or a happening or a run of events, given in writing, in a play, in a film, or on radio or television
examples: The film tells the story of a family that loses its farm.

oewn-06769768-n.learner: a small lie about something that does not matter much
examples: Sir William, how can you tell such a story?

connotation.why: names a lie in a softened, small-sounding way

oewn-01185006-v.learner: to give someone what they want or need, above all support, food, or the means of living
examples: He meant to provide for me amply, and thought he had done it.
the widow and younger children would by that means be provided for

oewn-00407888-v.learner: to do beforehand the things that something will need
examples: Mrs. Bennet had so carefully provided for the entertainment of her brother and sister.

oewn-02332196-v.learner: to give something useful or needed to someone
examples: The guide provided each of us with a map and a torch.

oewn-00981945-s.learner: done with little or no waiting
examples: Jane has written to beg my uncle's immediate assistance.
your assurance of it, I suppose, carried immediate conviction to him

oewn-00451113-s.learner: very near to something, or touching it, in space or in time
examples: Only the houses in the immediate neighbourhood of the river were flooded.

oewn-01584261-s.learner: coming right before or right after something in a chain of cause and result
examples: The immediate cause of the fire was a candle left burning.

oewn-00446005-s.learner: more distant from something, above all in degree
examples: His account was even further from the truth than hers.
Nothing could be further from her real feelings.

oewn-01485535-a.learner: not married, or having to do with not being married
examples: a single man in possession of a good fortune must be in want of a wife
It must make you better satisfied that your other four are single.

oewn-02221616-a.learner: being one on its own, or made up of only one thing, part, side, or person
examples: she executed six capital works, and has not left a single failure
It was not known that Wickham had a single relation with whom he kept up any connection.

oewn-00495505-a.learner: belonging to, or typical of, one thing or one person taken by itself
examples: Each single claim was judged on its own facts.

oewn-00036138-r.learner: to a fair extent or degree, but not fully
examples: I think she would have made a pretty good journey even in a black one
You know pretty well, I suppose, what has been done for the young people.

oewn-06845083-n.learner: the ninth letter of the Roman alphabet, the set of letters used to write English
examples: Remember to put a dot over the i.
There is an i in the middle of the word 'ship'.

oewn-01416084-a.learner: likely, though not sure, to be true or real or to come about
examples: his falling in love at all is not extremely probable
it is probable that he may spend very little of his time there in future

oewn-01414991-s.learner: seeming to be bound to come
examples: No one wished to think about the probable consequences of going on with the plan.

oewn-04694682-n.learner: the quality of being attractive, so that people are interested, pleased, or excited by it
examples: she has of course not counted in what was due to her own personal charm
Her home and her housekeeping, her parish and her poultry, and all their dependent concerns, had not yet lost their charms.

oewn-03013287-n.learner: a small object that people believe brings good luck
examples: She wore a silver charm on a chain and never took it off.

oewn-07174442-n.learner: a set of words that people believe has magic power when it is said
examples: The old woman muttered a charm over the sick child.
